topic: How are link budget margins calculated when accounting for time-varying rain attenuation versus fixed gaseous absorption losses?
consensus_response: When calculating link budget margins, it is essential to account for both time-varying rain attenuation and fixed gaseous absorption losses. Rain attenuation is the main impairment in Q/V band satellite feeder links, typically modeled using the lognormal distribution. The spatial correlation coefficient ρ affects the joint probability density function of correlated rain attenuations, impacting link availability and capacity trade-offs. Hybrid Fade Margin (HFM) combines fixed fade margin with uplink power control schemes to adapt to varying rain conditions, ensuring that the active gateway has the higher SNR. Rain Attenuation Modeling using Machine Learning (RAMML) can predict rain attenuation with high accuracy, adapting to specific climate zones and weather patterns.

The spatial correlation coefficient ρ affects the joint probability density function of correlated rain attenuations, impacting link availability and capacity trade-offs. A radiometer or rain gauge can improve the deduction of rain attenuation from total attenuation, reducing the fixed fade margin.
